items.title: 61530_Roy Eldridge oral history interview
items.q: all the cats used to come up there and sit in -- Dizzy, Joe Guy, Charlie, Bobby Moore, all the little trumpet players that was around in those days.

ctx.x: And I came to the Savoy, and all the cats used to come up there and sit in -- Dizzy, Joe Guy, Charlie, Bobby Moore, all the little trumpet players that was around in those days. And they know my records better than I did. They all knew the solos, I mean. So they would sit in.

And that's when I had my meeting with Joe Glaser. I had seen Joe Glaser once in Chicago, because that's when everybody...by me being on the air, everybody was taking notice of me then, you know. I had won those polls and things, and I was winning Second Place, and somebody said, "Well, why let a dead man beat him out all the time?" -- Bix was beating me out all the time, you know. They said, "How about people that's living?" So they turned around and they let me win First!
